title: Effective Noise Thresholds for Reliable Quantum Approximation Optimisation Algorithm under Noisy Environment
authors: Yozef Tjandra, Hendrik Santoso Sugiarto, Celine Vania Setiadi, Joanna Gracia Tan, Andriyan Bayu Suksmono
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms are leading candidates for practical utilisation on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) processors, but accumulating noise bounds the usefulness of circuit depths. For the quantum approximate optimisation algorithm (QAOA), this trade-off has mostly been addressed by searching for the best depth for a given device. In this work, we consider the inverse question: how much noise each depth can tolerate. Using GPU-accelerated noisy QAOA simulations for MaxCut on three graph families with 6 to 18 vertices, depths up to 10 and three noise channels, we fit the approximation ratios with a generalised logistic surface. We propose the effective noise threshold as the inflection boundary of the logistic surfaces, a noise boundary separating reliable and unreliable QAOA approximation regimes. In general, the threshold decreases as depth rises, indicating that deeper circuits demand for stricter noise requirement for reliable approximation. Its best and worst values over depth divide the noise axis into three regions: every depth remains effective, depth must be chosen with care, or no depth induces effective optimisation. Assessing on the ibm_marrakesh processor, although modelled gate errors understate factual noise, the threshold modeling remains beneficial in informing qualitative depth-dependence structure and identifying dominating noise channel in noisy QAOA.
summary: This work analyzes the noise resilience of the QAOA algorithm by calculating an 'effective noise threshold' for various circuit depths. By inverting the typical analysis, the authors show that deeper circuits require significantly lower noise levels to maintain reliable performance. This provides a critical diagnostic tool for benchmarking NISQ hardware for optimization problems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the inverse problem for QAOA: determining the maximum noise level a given circuit depth can tolerate, rather than finding the optimal depth for a fixed noise.
main_result: The effective noise threshold, $r_\star(p)$, generally decreases as the QAOA depth ($p$) increases, defining critical regimes for reliable quantum computation.
method: The authors simulate noisy QAOA circuits using GPU acceleration and fit the resulting approximation ratios to a generalized logistic surface to extract the inflection point, which defines the threshold.
model_or_system: The model uses the QAOA algorithm applied to the MaxCut problem on various graph families. Noise is incorporated via multiple channels (depolarizing, bit-flip, amplitude damping) acting on the quantum state evolution.
key_observables: Approximation Ratio (AR), Effective Noise Threshold ($r_\star(p)$), and the noise rate ($r$).
important_parameters: QAOA Depth ($p \in [1, 10]$), Noise Rate ($r$), and specific graph structures (ER, Path, Bipartite).
main_assumptions: The model assumes the noise can be characterized by fitting the AR to a generalized logistic function; hardware results are noted to understate the true noise due to modeling limitations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the noisy QAOA workflow and the 3D fitting of the noise threshold using a generalized logistic surface. Other figures show representative graph instances.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the noisy QAOA framework, then develops the methodology by fitting the AR vs. noise rate/depth to a logistic function to extract the noise threshold. Finally, it analyzes the implications of this threshold across different depth regimes and tests the model on hardware.
why_interesting: It provides a quantitative, depth-dependent metric ($r_\star(p)$) for assessing the practical limits of variational quantum algorithms on noisy hardware, which is crucial for designing fault-tolerant quantum algorithms.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
